units.translation: γάρ [for] inserted in a sentence whose cause it contains
unless φιλῶ γε κἀβδέλυκτ᾽ [I love and not loathsome] is to be written with Bekker.
γάρ [for] is repeated within a short space where the sentence which served to give a reason is to be confirmed, rarely in the same verse, as

more frequently in two or more verses following one another, as Pr. 294-296, Sept. 336 338, Pers. 168 169, 669 670 and others among the examples indicated above. But Ag. 559 εὐναὶ γὰρ ἦσαν δαΐων πρὸς τείχεσιν · ἐξ οὐρανοῦ γὰρ κἀπὸ γῆς λειμώνιαι δρόσοι κατεψάκαζον [for there were resting-places of the enemy against the walls; for from heaven and from earth meadow dews kept sprinkling down], Pearson rightly changed the second γάρ [for] to dé.
γάρ [for] in replying is not rarely referred to a sentence to be supplied in thought, as
i. e. you speak rightly: for complaints are of no avail.
where the interrogative sentence τί νιν στυγεῖς; [why do you hate him?] is equivalent to the affirmative μάτην νιν στυγεῖς [you hate him in vain].

The most frequent use of the particle is in interrogative sentences, not rarely after ἢ [or] or oὐ [not] or after interrogative pronouns and particles, τίς [who] τί [what] ποῖος [of what kind] ποῦ [where] πῆ [in what way] πῶς [how], placed, in which themselves too, when the interrogation is removed, it retains its explanatory force. Thus ἢ γὰρ [or for] – Pr. 745 757 974. Ag. 1366. οὐ γὰρ [not for] — Pr. 987. Pers. 798. πότερα γὰρ [whether for] - Pers. 239. Ag. 630. ποῦ γὰρ [where for] – Eum. 427. πῶς γὰρ [how for] – Ag. 634 1374. Ch. 187. Eum. 607 652. τίνα γὰρ [whom for] – Sept 771. τί γὰρ [what for] – Pr. 519 1056. Ag. 272 601 1139 1239 1486. Ch. 48 388 880. Eum. 211 678. Fr. 174. πῶς γὰρ οὐ; [how for not?] Ch. 754. || In wishing. εἰ γὰρ [if for] — Pr. 152. Ch. 345. εἴθε γὰρ [would that for] – Sept. 566.
